HTML §2.5.3 gives every element including HTMLOrSVGElement a nonce whose setter writes the [[CryptographicNonce]] slot and NOT the content attribute, which is what keeps a header-delivered policy's nonce out of a CSS selector. AngleSharp declares one attribute-backed property, on this interface alone, whose setter writes the attribute; skipped so the reflected HTMLElement.nonce row is what every element answers with.

HTML names the IDL attribute scrollAmount (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/obsolete.html#htmlmarqueeelement); AngleSharp's [DomName] on IHtmlMarqueeElement.ScrollAmount is the CONTENT attribute's all-lower-case spelling, so the projection was a nonstandard member under a name no page can use. The reflected scrollAmount row replaces it.
The same [DomName] casing defect on IHtmlMarqueeElement.ScrollDelay, and the reflected scrollDelay row beside it.

HTML's meta element has a charset content attribute but no charset IDL attribute (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#the-meta-element). AngleSharp 1.7.3 adds DomName to its CLR convenience property; do not expose a new nonstandard JavaScript member.
